audience: DCCE (กรม สส.) executives and policy owners reading the Executive Summary Report
decision_use: Understand where CRDB's output sits in the software/data-platform development lifecycle, what ready-to-build artifacts it hands over, and how Content Writer and Software Developer responsibilities split so the next phase can start implementation immediately rather than repeating discovery
section_job: Position the project in the Reference Integrated Data and Web Platform SDLC (6 phases; CRDB raises phase 1 coverage from ~35% to ~70% and phase 2 from ~40% to ~80%), present the 4-5 ready-to-build artifacts (Sitemap v9, DRD v2, Storyboard v2, Business Narratives, CDM/DMF), and set the Content Writer vs Software Developer role split -- without presuming knowledge of the next TOR's actual content
target_altitude: Executive narrative naming the 6 SDLC phases and coverage percentages, listing the ready-to-build artifacts with their scale (38 nodes, 75 requirements, etc.), no per-page storyboard or DRD table detail
report_specific_rules: Full Thai+English agency name at first mention ("กรมการเปลี่ยนแปลงสภาพภูมิอากาศและสิ่งแวดล้อม"), then only "กรม สส." thereafter -- never bare "สส." without "กรม" leading it
Never bare English "NCAIF" -- give the full Thai name at first mention, then use "โครงสร้างข้อมูลด้านการปรับตัวฯ" or "โครงสร้างข้อมูล NCAIF"
No internal jargon abbreviations (TOR70, CRDB) without spelling out at first use

No internal document locators (slide numbers, page numbers, superseded internal section references) in narrative prose -- cite by document name, E-xxx evidence code, or named standard; locators live in evidence-traceability only

Use "คณะที่ปรึกษา" as the active subject for study/survey/interview/workshop/analysis/synthesis/design-decision sentences; avoid passive voice or "โครงการ" as actor except for contractual objective/scope statements
Countable parallel items formatted as numbered/bulleted lists with substantive descriptions, not run-on prose
Executive-summary substance retention: cut operational/technical detail but never reduce a point to one floating sentence; each subsection needs Why/What/So-What in 1-2 paragraphs
Formal official vocabulary ("ข้อมูลอภิพันธ์"/"ข้อมูลกำกับ", "สถาปัตยกรรมสารสนเทศ", "ธรรมาภิบาลข้อมูล"); avoid colloquial phrasing

No contrastive/justify-by-flaw scaffolding -- never justify a point by first negating a bad alternative ("แทนที่จะ...", "เพื่อป้องกัน...", "เพื่อลดความเสี่ยง...", "หลีกเลี่ยง..."); state findings and their implications directly

Hard constraint from the plan (verbatim): "ห้ามเขียนในลักษณะที่รู้แล้วว่า TOR โครงการฉบับถัดไปมีเนื้อหาอย่างไร" -- never write as though the next procurement's TOR content is already known; frame ready-to-build artifacts as reducing discovery risk for whatever the next project turns out to be, not as predictions about its text
inclusions: position in the Reference Integrated Data and Web Platform SDLC (6 phases: Requirements Elicitation & Analysis, Functional Analysis & Solution Design, Implementation, System Integration Verification & Validation, Deployment & Operational Transition, Operations/Maintenance/Continuous Improvement); CRDB raises phase 1 coverage from ~35% to ~70% and phase 2 from ~40% to ~80% (independent assessment)

the 4-5 ready-to-build artifacts: Sitemap v9 (38 nodes, 4 categories), DRD v2 (75 requirements, 13 deliverables, 9 service briefs, 12 data specs), Storyboard v2 (38-page wireframes with Source-Content Mapping), WP6 Business Narratives, CDM/DMF (8 domains, 12-field metadata, 74-term glossary)
Content Writer vs Software Developer role split: Content Writer closes the 33 content gaps per Storyboard; Software Developer builds CMS validation rules, data pipelines, and UI per DRD v2
brief, concise scoping suggestion for the next project phase, ahead of the detail that belongs in section 4.4
exclusions: any claim or implication about the next TOR's actual content (hard constraint above)
evidence_policy: Use verified figures from WP4 Sitemap v9, WP4 Developer-Ready DRD v2, WP4 Node Content Storyboard v2, WP6 Service Business Narratives, WP5 Data Management Framework Report, and the TOR70 SDLC storyline document (the Reference Integrated Data and Web Platform SDLC's primary source) in prose; keep internal locators and per-source detail in the evidence-traceability sidecar
required_concepts: Reference Integrated Data and Web Platform SDLC, 6 phases, synthesized from TOGAF/IBM Data Architecture/Australian National Archives/BrowserStack
Discovery Trap -- the risk CRDB's ready-to-build package is designed to prevent for the next contractor
Logic Invention risk -- why the Content Writer/Developer role split exists
